To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the radio emission in submillimetre-selected galaxies is extended on scales of several kiloparsec and that there is a low fraction of active galactic nuclei among them.

(i) SMGs are more spatially extended than the µJy radio source population, (ii) they have sizes comparable to those of local ULIRGs, (iii) they are less likely to host an AGN, and (iv) they are less clustered than the general radio source population.

submillimetre luminous starburst galaxies are larger than local UL IRGs, have a lower incidence of active galactic nuclei and, unlike the fainter radio sources in GOODS-N, are not extended on scales of 1–4 arcsec.
